info.name: blt API
info.description:
blt collects backup jobs and inventory from backup products (Commvault,
Rubrik) into one database. **This API is the only thing that reads or
writes that database.** Collectors never touch Postgres: they ask the API
where they left off, post what they collected, and report how the run
went. Reports and other readers use the same API.

## Signing in

Every endpoint except `/healthz` needs the API key in an `X-API-Key`
header. In these docs: **Authorize** (top right), paste the key, and the
*Try it out* buttons send it.

```
curl -H "X-API-Key: $BLT_API_KEY" \
    https://api.blt.lab.ethos.home/v1/sources/commvault/cv-toaster/last-run
```

## Conventions

- **Sources are named in the path**:
  `/v1/sources/{source type}/{source name}/...` - a CommCell is
  `/v1/sources/commvault/cv-toaster`, an RSC account
  `/v1/sources/rubrik/work`. The name is blt's own (its Prefect
  block's), not the product's. Each source type has its own endpoints
  below that, in its product's own terms.
- **Times** are ISO 8601 with a time zone (`2026-10-29T14:00:00Z`). A
  time in a request body without one is refused.
- **Lists** page with `limit` and `offset`.
- **Errors** come back as `{"detail": "..."}`: 401 for a missing or wrong
  key, 404 for an unknown source, run or job, 422 for a body or
  parameter that does not validate.
- **Writes are upserts**, keyed by the source's own ids. Posting the same
  batch twice changes nothing; a batch collected *before* what is
  already stored is ignored, so a slow run cannot roll a job back.

## Versions

Everything except `/healthz` is under `/v1`. Changes that don't break a
client (a new endpoint, field or optional parameter) are made in `/v1`
as it stands. A change that would break one goes into a `/v2` beside
it, and `/v1` stays until every collector has moved over.

## One collection run

1. `GET .../last-run` - the watermark: where the last successful run
   started. None means never collected.
2. `POST .../runs` - open a run; keep its `id`.
3. `POST .../jobs` - the jobs collected, in batches, each with the run id.
4. `POST .../runs/{run_id}/finish` - succeeded or failed. Only a
   succeeded run moves the watermark.

Commvault runs also check on jobs still active (`GET .../jobs?active=true`)
and reconcile ones the CommCell no longer knows (`PATCH .../jobs/{job_id}`).
Rubrik runs need neither: RSC reports every change, so one pass covers it.

request.description: Every product's failed jobs since `since` (an ISO time, e.g. 2026-11-10T00:00:00Z).
Every job still running, any product.

item.name: Job counts by state, per source

request.description: How many jobs ended each way, per source, since `since`.
Every storage target with its latest use.
Every source, its collector, its timing and next starts; secrets only as set or not.
Are runs getting through: slots taken against runs collecting, and stuck runs.
Starts the source's check on its collector; follow it with GET /v1/admin/runs/{id}.
Turns collection on for a source (false: off).

`{"status": "ok"}` once the API can query its database. No key
needed: this is what the liveness and readiness probes call.

Every CommCell and RSC account blt has collected from, of any
product, with the id that stands for it everywhere. A source
appears the first time a run is started for it.

Jobs from every source, newest start first (jobs not yet started
first of all). The `X-Total-Count` header holds how many match,
for paging.

Jobs per state for each group, newest day first. Takes the same
filters as `GET /v1/jobs`; jobs not yet started have no day.

One job in the common shape, with the product's full record of
it in `product`.

item.name: Every storage target, with its latest use and trend

request.description:
Each target with its newest sample and, once there are enough
hours of samples, how fast it is filling and when it would be
full at that rate.

item.name: Where NetBackup's data goes: backups and copies per pool

request.description:
For the Storage page's Sankey: what each NetBackup primary's
backups wrote into each disk pool, and what was copied from one
pool to another - duplicated on one primary, or replicated to
another (matched to that primary's import of the same image) -
with every pool's use and trend. Bytes as the jobs report them,
before deduplication.

With `primary`, that primary's copies only, in three columns: the
pool each is read from, the SLP that made it, and the pool it
lands in (on that primary or the one it replicates to).
The target, present or not, with its latest sample and trend.

Oldest first. `every=day` gives one sample a day (the last of
it), for long ranges.

Every storage target the collector read from the source, each
with its capacity and use at `collected_at`. A target is matched
by `product_key`; one not seen before is added. With `complete`
(the default), targets the source no longer lists are marked not
present - their samples stay.

Every storage target the collector read from the source, each
with its capacity and use at `collected_at`. A target is matched
by `product_key`; one not seen before is added. With `complete`
(the default), targets the source no longer lists are marked not
present - their samples stay.

Every CommCell, Rubrik account and NetBackup primary Prefect
holds a block for, with whether each secret is set - never its
value.

Saves the primary's block. Collection starts off: check the
primary first (`.../check`), then turn `collect` on.

item.name: Add a CommCell or Commvault Cloud tenant

request.description:
Saves the CommCell's block: a user name and password, or a
token pair from Command Center (renewed into the block from then
on). Collection starts off: check it first (`.../check`), then
turn `collect` on.

item.name: Add a Rubrik Security Cloud account

request.description:
Saves the account's block from its service account file's
fields. The secret is kept in the block and never shown again; the
file is not needed after. Collection starts off: check it first
(`.../check`), then turn `collect` on.

Changes only what is given: `collect`, `collector` and
`verify_tls` for any source, and each product's own fields for its
sources (a 422 for another product's). New credentials replace the
old ones whole; check the source again after.

Removes the block, so nothing collects from it any more. What
was collected stays in blt.

item.name: Check a source, from a worker

request.description:
Starts the product's check for the source, on the collector
that reaches it: it signs in with what the block holds and tries
each read blt makes - storage, jobs, and for NetBackup its SLP
images, for Rubrik inventory and SLA domains - logging one OK or
FAIL line for each. Watch the run's log.

item.name: Fetch a NetBackup primary's CA certificate, from a worker

request.description:
Starts blt-netbackup-fetch-ca: it asks the primary for its CA
certificate (which needs no sign-in) and logs it with its SHA-256
fingerprint. Compare the fingerprint with the primary's own
(`nbcertcmd -displayCACertDetail`) before trusting it.

item.name: The workers that collect, and whether each is there

request.description:
blt's own worker and every remote collector: each work queue in
blt's pool, and each collector a source names, with when it last
asked for work and the sources it reaches.

Every deployment, with its schedules, its last finished run and
its next scheduled one.

Starts a run now, with these parameters over its defaults. A
run for one source (a `commcell`, `account` or `primary`
parameter) goes to the collector that reaches that source.

No scheduled runs until it is resumed. It stays paused when the
worker restarts and deploys prefect.yaml again (prefect deploy
leaves `paused` alone when prefect.yaml does not set it).
Its schedules make runs again.

Flow runs by when they were due, newest first: every
deployment's, or one's.

The collection slots against the runs that could hold them, and
the runs that look stuck. A slot is leaked when a run that held it
is gone - its worker restarted, or the Prefect server did while it
kept them only in memory - and runs then queue for it for ever.

item.name: Cancel stuck runs and give back leaked slots

request.description:
Cancels the runs asked for that are still stuck by the same
rule - at once, since no worker is running them - and then, if
Prefect counts more slots taken than there are runs collecting,
brings the count down to those runs. It never goes below them, so
a run that holds a slot keeps it.

item.name: A flow run and its log

request.description:
The run and its log lines, oldest first. Poll with `log_offset`
set to the lines already shown to get only new ones.

Asks the worker to stop the run: it goes to CANCELLING, then
CANCELLED once the worker has stopped it.

item.name: Where the last collection got to

request.description:
The CommCell's watermark and its most recent run. An unknown
CommCell is not an error: it comes back with no watermark, which
tells a collector to start with an initial run.

item.name: How far back history has been collected

request.description:
Where the next backfill chunk should end, and whether backfill
has reached the start of the CommCell's history.
Called by the backfill flow after each chunk it collects.

Opens a run (status `running`) and returns it; send its `id`
with each batch of jobs or objects. The CommCell is created on its
first run.

Records how the run went. A succeeded collection run (initial,
delta or full) becomes the new watermark. A succeeded inventory
run marks everything it did not list as no longer present, and
stores that day's per-instance report, and points jobs at the
clients they ran on (common.job.source_object_id).

Inserts new jobs and updates known ones, keyed by Commvault's
job id. A job collected earlier than what is stored is left alone.
`written` counts the jobs actually inserted or changed.

Jobs in job id order. The collector uses `active=true` to find
jobs to check on, and `unseen_in_run` to find ones to reconcile.

One job by Commvault's job id, with its full Commvault record in
`raw`.

Used to mark a job the CommCell no longer knows as "Not found in
CommCell"; anything Commvault can still describe goes through
`POST .../jobs`.

Clients, instances and databases as the CommCell lists them,
during an inventory run. Parents go before their children: clients,
then instances, then databases.
What the CommCell says exists, by kind then name.

item.name: SQL Server instances: discovered vs backed up

request.description:
Databases discovered against databases backed up, per SQL
Server instance, for its most recent full backup.

Is everything this source says exists also backed up?

Judged entirely from the source's own inventory (see
ValidationReport for what that can and cannot establish), with
each database's last backup job looked up in the job table as a
second opinion on whether that backup actually succeeded.

item.name: Where the last collection got to

request.description:
The account's watermark and its most recent job run. An unknown
account is not an error: no watermark means do an initial run.
Inventory runs do not count.

Opens a run (status `running`); send its `id` with each batch.
The account is created on its first run.

Records how the run went. A succeeded job run becomes the new
watermark; a succeeded inventory run marks every object it did not
list as no longer present, and points jobs at the objects they ran
on (common.job.source_object_id).

Inserts new jobs and updates known ones, keyed by `series_key`.
A job collected earlier than what is stored is left alone.
Jobs, most recently updated first.
One job by its series key, with RSC's full record in `raw`.

Objects as RSC lists them, during an inventory run, keyed by
`source_key`.
What RSC says exists, by type then name.

item.name: Where the last job collection got to

request.description:
The primary's watermark and its most recent job run. An unknown
primary is not an error: no watermark means do an initial run.

Opens a run (status `running`); send its `id` with each batch.
The primary is created on its first run.

Records how the run went. A succeeded run becomes the new
watermark.

Inserts new jobs and updates known ones, keyed by `job_id`. A job
collected earlier than what is stored is left alone.
Jobs, most recently updated first.

item.name: Store every SLP of the primary

request.description:
The primary's storage lifecycle policies, all of them: each is
stored as sent, and SLPs not in the batch are removed. A batch
older than what is stored is left alone.
Its storage lifecycle policies as last collected, by name.
One job by its id, with NetBackup's full record in `raw`.
